title: revloop resolve intent
description: What the resolve leg returns. It is intent for the orchestrator to act on, never a record of what the agent already did — the agent holds no GitHub credential and makes no GitHub call. Carries the same two harness-forced shapes as the findings schema: no $schema or $id key, because Claude Code's --json-schema rejects a schema naming the 2020-12 meta-schema; and every property listed in 'required', because Codex enforces OpenAI strict mode. Optional fields are nullable rather than absent.

blocked.description: True when the leg could not do its job at all. Terminates the loop.

blocked_reason.description: Why, or null. Only meaningful when blocked is true.

summary.description: The summary comment body, in Markdown, explaining what was fixed, skipped, deferred and rebutted. Written for a collaborator who has never heard of revloop. The orchestrator appends the alert, the disposition table, the run details, the machine-readable marker and any 'Deferred work filed' list; do not write any of them yourself.

dispositions.description: Exactly one entry per finding supplied in the prompt, no more and no fewer. Every finding gets one, whatever its severity — severity governs what happens after verification, never whether verification happens. The orchestrator checks the coverage: a finding left out has no reply and its thread is never resolved, which is a silent loss rather than a visible one.

finding_number.description: The number shown beside the finding in the prompt — 1 for the first, 2 for the second, and so on. A small integer rather than the finding's id, because copying a 16-character hash accurately is clerical work models are poor at and a mistyped one is accepted silently. The id is still printed beside the number for quoting in prose.

disposition.description: fixed: code changed. skipped: not acting by policy, such as a finding below the pass's min_fix_severity threshold. deferred: real, worth doing, not here — persists to a sink. rebutted: technically wrong for this codebase. escalated: needs a human decision, applies revloop/stop and leaves the thread open.

reply.description: The in-thread reply body to post. Always required: nothing is silently dropped, and a finding skipped for being below the threshold still gets a one-line reason. Start with the reason, not with the disposition — the orchestrator prepends 'Fixed.', 'Deferred.' and the rest. Earlier replies quoted back to you in the prompt already carry that lead, and repeating it is how a comment ends up reading 'Fixed. Fixed.'

persist.description: For a deferred defect worth recording outside this PR, the issue to file. Null for every other disposition. Write it to stand alone for someone who never saw the PR.

title.description: One line naming the defect, as an issue title rather than a review comment.

body.description: What the defect is, where, why it matters, and what fixing it would involve. Measure before asserting: a headline number that turns out to be mostly unrelated makes the issue misleading.

duplicate_of.description: The number of an existing issue that already covers this defect, chosen from the candidates supplied in the prompt. Null when none of them match, and null when none were supplied — the orchestrator rejects a number it did not offer, because commenting on an unrelated issue and resolving the thread against it is worse than filing a duplicate. Ambiguity between two supplied candidates counts as a match: a missed filing still has the PR thread behind it, while a duplicate is mess someone has to clean up.
